comments.body:
We need to isolate which layer is breaking down here. Downward, below MHLO, types should be fully translated to signless (where the operations carry sign information where needed).

I expect that this is just at our Python layer taking the signless type in the signature and mapping that to a signed dtype when producing the array. If this is true, bitcasting to the expected unsigned dtype should show that the computation was done properly.

The last step of converting an IREE internal ElementType to dtype happens here: https://github.com/openxla/iree/blob/main/runtime/bindings/python/hal.cc#L439

I expect we will find that this is decoding IREE_HAL_ELEMENT_TYPE_INT_32 (signless int32) as a signed int32 and that we are not setting the ElementType to a fully signed dtype in the compiler. I'd need to dig into where we do that but would be good to know if the hypothesis holds.

Hi @stellaraccident, thanks for the response and suggestions!
Your hypothesis about the python mappings looks to be correct. The element type is coming in as `IREE_HAL_ELEMENT_TYPE_INT_32` which is mapped to `type_code = i`. If I hardcode the `type_code = I`, the output type is now correctly `uint32` when I run the script.  In either case, the computation is correct if the output is bitcasted.
I believe Rob is looking at this one actively.
I added additional details to the duplicate that exists in the JAX integration work: https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/12665

issue.body:
Repro:
```
import platform
import iree.compiler
import iree.runtime
import numpy as np

CODE = """
#loc0 = loc(unknown)
module @jit_prim_fun.0 {
  func.func public @main(%arg0: tensor<5x7xui32> loc(unknown)) -> tensor<5x7xui32> {
    %0 = "mhlo.sort"(%arg0) ({
    ^bb0(%arg1: tensor<ui32> loc(unknown), %arg2: tensor<ui32> loc(unknown)):
      %1 = "mhlo.compare"(%arg1, %arg2) {compare_type = #mhlo<"comparison_type UNSIGNED">, comparison_direction = #mhlo<"comparison_direction LT">} : (tensor<ui32>, tensor<ui32>) -> tensor<i1> loc(#loc2)
      "mhlo.return"(%1) : (tensor<i1>) -> () loc(#loc1)
    }) {dimension = 1 : i64, is_stable = false} : (tensor<5x7xui32>) -> tensor<5x7xui32> loc(#loc1)
    return %0 : tensor<5x7xui32> loc(#loc0)
  } loc(#loc0)
} loc(#loc0)
#loc1 = loc("jit(sort)/jit(main)/sort[dimension=1 is_stable=False num_keys=1]"("/Users/phawkins/p/jax/tests/lax_test.py":2039:1))
#loc2 = loc("jit(sort)/jit(main)/lt"("/Users/phawkins/p/jax/tests/lax_test.py":2039:1))
"""

# Work around https://github.com/google/iree/issues/9028
extra_args = []
if platform.system() == "Darwin" and platform.machine() == "arm64":
  extra_args += ["--iree-llvm-target-triple=arm64-apple-darwin21.5.0"]

iree_config = iree.runtime.system_api.Config("dylib")
iree_binary = iree.compiler.compile_str(
    CODE, target_backends=["dylib"], input_type="mhlo", extra_args=extra_args)
vm_module = iree.runtime.VmModule.from_flatbuffer(iree_binary)
module_object = iree.runtime.load_vm_module(vm_module, iree_config)

out = module_object["main"](np.ones((5, 7), dtype=np.uint32))
assert out.dtype == np.uint32, out.dtype
```

Get:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/phawkins/p/jax/t.py", line 34, in <module>
    assert out.dtype == np.uint32, out.dtype
AssertionError: int32
```

The MHLO has a ui32 output, so I expect a uint32 result from IREE.

milestone.description:
Set of work to make IREE compliant as a JAX [PjRt](https://github.com/openxla/openxla-pjrt-plugin) backend.
This will include both PJRT plugin integration, validating correctness of the IREE compiler, and planning JAX
specific feature work for IREE. The majority of this work will focus on front-end compatibility but could
include compilation failures further in the CPU / GPU backends.

issue.body:
Thanks so much to @rsuderman for the guidance and help !

This PR solves a bug where the signedness of inputs and outputs is lost, because lowering to linalg dialect throws the signedness away. To fix it, I'm using a new op `tensor.bitcast`, which casts the inputs/outputs of the function from an unsigned type to the signless type in the body.

I am completely new to IREE, so this PR is still a little rough. Any critique and suggestions for improvement is highly welcome. I'm particularly interested in ways to make this more robust.

Fixes #9282
Fixes #12665
